Hi Monica & Kimberly,

I need a quick governance check on a PIP I plan to initiate for Jake Myers in Data Platform. Before I share anything with Jake or his manager track, I want HR and Legal sign-off on the template and the proposed timeline (30 days, weekly checkpoints).

Background in one line: repeated missed SLA ownership on the data export pipelines after two informal coaching cycles; manager (Laura) and I agreed PIP is the next step. Laura is on cc and can add context as needed.

What I’m asking for:
- HR: confirm the attached PIP template meets Redwood’s internal requirements (language around expectations, reasonable accommodations, and manager support). If there are any mandatory steps I’ve missed, flag them.
- Legal: quick review for any potentially problematic phrasing around termination triggers and confidentiality language.

Attachments: PIP_StepZero_Jake_Myers_v1.docx (draft)

Timeline: I’d like to get sign-off by EOD Tuesday (tomorrow) so we can meet with Jake Wednesday morning. If that’s infeasible, tell me the blocker and a realistic ETA.

Markers: please reply with edits in-line or the redlined doc. If you want me to route differently (people ops lead), say so.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround on something sensitive.

— Markus

Thanks Markus — I can take point on HR checks. Quick notes after a first pass of the draft you attached:

1) Checklist items (HR must confirm before manager meeting):
   - Documentation of prior coaching conversations attached to the PIP file (please confirm dates).
   - Performance goals are measurable and time-bound (your draft has them, we may make language tighter).
   - Reasonable accommodations: include a line directing managers to pause and check with People Ops if a medical or disability accommodation is disclosed.
   - Opt-in for an independent HR observer at the kickoff meeting (recommended for sensitive cases).

2) Timeline advice: 30 days is reasonable for delivery-level misses, but include a mid-point checkpoint at day 15 for documented feedback.

3) Communication plan: add a short paragraph we can read aloud at the meeting to set expectations and maintain the factual tone.

I’m attaching a small HR-side edit (attachment name: PIP_StepZero_Jake_Myers_v1.docx — tracked changes). Also: do you have the log of the two prior coaching emails? We’ll need that as evidence.

If you want me to join the kickoff, I can be available Wednesday morning (09:00–11:00 PT).

— Monica
People Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

Markus/Monica — I reviewed the updated draft in Drive. Two quick legal notes:

1) Termination trigger language: the phrasing in section 4.2 reads as an automatic termination on failure to meet metrics. Replace with a rubric-based escalation: failure to meet measures at the end of the PIP should trigger a documented senior-review and final HR sign-off before separation. That reduces exposure.

2) Confidentiality: tighten the confidentiality paragraph to make clear that PIP contents are confidential internal records and cannot be shared externally; however, any disclosures required by subpoena or statutory rights are excluded.

I attached a redline (PIP_StepZero_Jake_Myers_v1_redline.docx) with the exact language changes. None of these are blockers for the kickoff — implement the two tweaks and you’ll have my sign-off.

— Kimberly
